verbalization: Prednisone is implicated in the pathogenesis of hematologic cancer through a series of interconnected mechanisms. The evidence suggests that Prednisone causes Dry Scalp, which is then influenced by Alitretinoin or Prednisolone, both of which are classified as immunotherapeutic agents and therapeutic glucocorticoids. These agents are known to have anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive properties, which may contribute to the suppression of hematologic cancer progression. The lowest common ancestors of Prednisone and its metabolites—Immunotherapeutic Agents and Therapeutic Glucocorticoids—highlight a shared biological role in modulating immune responses and cellular homeostasis. While the direct causal link between Prednisone and hematologic cancer remains indirect, the cumulative evidence points to a potential role of glucocorticoid-mediated pathways in the development of this disease. The integration of these pathways underscores the importance of considering steroid hormones in the context of cancer biology, particularly in relation to immune modulation and inflammatory regulation.
